items.backtranslation: A manager/person in charge is required
items.problem: "Owner" here is the person who owns the action (the responsible person), not a manager. "umphathi" (manager) is a wrong term and is inconsistent with "Umntu onoxanduva" used for "Responsible person" elsewhere.
"Seedlings" translated as "Izithole", which a farmer reads as the young of animals (calves, cubs), not young plants. Wrong term (plant vs animal).

items.english: Record a skill demonstrated in the garden separately from course completion or attendance.
items.draft: Bhala isakhono esibonisiweyo egadini ngokwahlukileyo kukugqiba ikhosi okanye ukuzimasa.
items.backtranslation: Record a skill shown in the garden separately from finishing a course or "ukuzimasa" (unclear word)
items.problem: "attendance" is rendered as "ukuzimasa", which is not a word for attendance and is unintelligible; the fact that the skill record is separate from attendance is lost.
items.corrected: Bhala isakhono esibonisiweyo egadini ngokwahlukileyo kukugqiba ikhosi okanye ukuba khona.

items.problem: "yabelwana" is not a correct form (neither passive "yabelwe" nor reciprocal "yabelana"); grammar garbled for an assessment state label. Coordinator: kept; -abelwana (shared with others) is the right form for "shared"; "yabelwe" would read as "was assigned".

items.english: Print a clean base map (boundary, house outlines and contours, no hatching) to sketch your design by hand
items.draft: Shicilela imephu esisiseko ecocekileyo (umda, imiphetho yezindlu nemigca yokuphakama, ngaphandle kwemigca yomthunzi) ukuze uzobe uyilo lwakho ngesandla
items.backtranslation: Print a clean base map (boundary, edges of houses and contour lines, without shade lines) so that you draw your design by hand
items.problem: isiZulu word "izindlu" used; isiXhosa is "iindlu" (house outlines).
items.corrected: Shicilela imephu esisiseko ecocekileyo (umda, imiphetho yeendlu nemigca yokuphakama, ngaphandle kwemigca yomthunzi) ukuze uzobe uyilo lwakho ngesandla

items.problem: "Min safe level" (minimum safe tank level) rendered as "safe low level", which reads as if a low level is safe; the minimum/threshold meaning is lost (water safety). Inconsistent with "Ubuncinci obukhuselekileyo" used for "Min safe" in the next line.
